name: Coleman Ski Descent
descent_text: Ski or walk off by the way you came up. From the summit plateau drop down the Roman Wall, a snow slope of 35 to 45 degrees that is usually downclimbed or skied with care when it is icy, onto the Deming Glacier. Cross the saddle and ski the Coleman Glacier's upper slopes, picking a line through its crevasses and icefall; snow bridges sag in afternoon sun, and late season can force an end-run to climbers' left. Aim for the Hogsback and the climbers' trail junction near 4,700 ft, then follow Trail 677 out. Cloud can close in fast, so follow your up-track.
approach: Start at the Heliotrope Ridge trailhead (about 3,700 ft) at the end of Glacier Creek Road (FR 39) and follow Trail 677 through old growth, crossing several creeks that run higher in the afternoon than the morning. At about two miles and 4,700 ft you pass the former Kulshan Cabin site, then a signed junction: the left fork goes to the Coleman Glacier overlook and the right fork is the climbers' trail. Take the climbers' trail steeply up the Hogsback moraine ridge to the edge of the Coleman Glacier near 6,000 ft, where most parties camp. In winter and spring the road may be gated miles short of the trailhead, which adds distance, and the glacier is skinned from there toward the Deming.
